references.text: Moses and Aaron rebelled against the Lord's command at the waters of Meribah, illustrating the consequences of rebelling against the Lord.
Moses encourages the people not to fear their enemies because the Lord goes before them, the same message given by Caleb and Joshua.
The people must not fear the nations in the land because the Lord is in their midst.
Joshua receives the same command not to fear because the Lord is with him wherever he goes.
David does not fear evil because the Lord is with him, paralleling the promise that the Lord is with Israel.
"The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?" This is the same declaration of trust expressed by Caleb and Joshua.
"Do not be afraid, for I am with you." God's promise of presence removes the fear of enemies.
Rahab confirms that the inhabitants of the land have lost courage because of Israel; their protection (shadow) is gone.
Warning against rebelling against the angel of the Lord who goes before the people.
Jesus teaches his disciples not to fear those who can kill the body, the same principle of trusting God rather than fearing humans.
"If God is for us, who can be against us?" Paul expresses the same confidence as Caleb and Joshua.
"The Lord is my helper; I will not fear. What can man do to me?"
